title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Tennessee Titans D/ST has field day against Colts
items.desc: The Tennessee Titans D/ST racked up two picks, a fumble recovery, six sacks, and a punt blocked for a touchdown in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
items.impact: The Titans' defense really stepped up on Sunday against their division rivals, with a huge blocked punt recovered in the endzone to put the team ahead in the game. Jeffery Simmons and Jermaine Johnson both had multiple sacks, putting pressure on Colts QB Daniel Jones all day. They still have a long way to go to be a relevant team, but it's a huge morale boost regardless.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Joey Slye has big game in win over Colts
items.desc: Joey Slye hit all four of his field goal attempts and both of his PATs in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
items.impact: Slye was able to get a bunch of points thanks to the Titans' offense being uable to find paydirt for most of the afternoon. The defense was also able to offer short fields to the offense as well, furthering Slye's chances of racking up points. He's an iffy start on a team that has struggled so much to score, but maybe they can build off of this and become interesting.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Tyjae Spears quiet in win over Colts
items.desc: Tyjae Spears ran once for a yard and caught his only target for three yards in the Titans' 26-20 win over Indianapolis on Sunday.
items.impact: A week after catching nine passes, Spears was nearly wiped out of the game plan for Tennessee. It's tough to trust Spears moving forward, and he's best left on waivers.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Tommy Tremble scores pair of TDs in Week 6
items.desc: Carolina Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble caught two touchdowns on four targets in a 25-14 Week 6 win.
items.impact: Tremble had four receptions for 46 yards and now has 4+ targets in every game this season except one. He also has 40+ yards in two games and caught the first two touchdowns of his season.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Darren Waller blanked in Week 6
items.desc: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller did not record a reception on two targets in a Week 6 win over Philadelphia.
items.impact: Waller's two targets were his fewest since Week 1. He had 14 between Weeks 3 and 4 heading into a Week 5 bye, but tight end Tommy Tremble got involved with two touchdowns in Week 6. The Panthers' offense has been potent, but Tremble has been involved as well with 11 catches in the last three games.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Wan'Dale Robinson snags three passes in win
items.desc: Wan'Dale Robinson caught three of seven targets for 22 yards in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
items.impact: Robinson and Carnell Tate were the only pass catchers to catch more than one pass from Cam Ward on Sunday, and also the only two to go over 10 yards. Robinson has had some usable performances this year, but they seem to come on an every-other-week basis.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Carnell Tate snags touchdown in win over Colts
items.desc: Carnell Tate caught six of seven targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
items.impact: Titans QB Cam Ward threw for 11 completions and 107 yards in this contest, meaning Tate accounted for over 50% of his completions and 65% of his passing yards. Only four Titans caught a pass on Sunday, and only Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson went over 10 yards. Tate has been a volume magnet so far this year, and it looks like he will continue to be. He's closing in on WR2 territory, but Ward's inconsistency will keep his floor low.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Jalen Coker has game-high 97 yards vs. Eagles
items.desc: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker caught six passes for 97 yards while seeing a season-high 13 targets in Week 6.
items.impact: Coker has at least nine targets in every game he has finished this season, forming an impressive tandem with second-year star Tetairoa McMillan. He had two touchdowns in Week 1 and has not scored since, but Carolina's passing attack has been impressive, and more will come in the future.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Tony Pollard runs for 76 yards in win
items.desc: Tony Pollard ran 19 times for 76 yards in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts. He failed to bring in his only target.
items.impact: Pollard had the backfield virtually all to himself, aside from Tyjae Spears getting a single carry. A touchdown or some receiving work would have helped Pollard's bottom line tremendously, but it was not meant to be. If anything, his volume seems to be solid, so he's an RB3 with upside.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Tetairoa McMillan gains 86 yards in Week 6 win
items.desc: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan caught six passes for 86 yards in a Week 6 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: McMillan has 75+ yards and 8+ targets in four of five games to start the season, a reliable floor in what has been a potent Carolina passing offense. He has not caught a touchdown yet with wide receiver Jalen Coker in the lineup, but McMillan's large frame and target rate indicate more could come in the future after scoring seven as a rookie.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Cam Ward completes 11 passes in win over Colts
items.desc: Cam Ward completed 11-of-22 passes for 102 yards, a touchdown, and a pick in the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts. He also ran three times for seven yards.
items.impact: Ward was not great in this game, a theme throughout this season. However, outside of his interception, he stayed out of trouble, not taking a single sack. He's outside of streaming consideration until he shows some sign of improvement.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Indianapolis Colts D/ST posts interception in loss
items.desc: The Indianapolis Colts D/ST posted an interception in the team's 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday. They didn't put up anything else in the box score.
items.impact: The Colts continue to get run over by other teams, if you can call what the Titans did to them "running over." It was more the Titans' defense doing the damage than their offense, but it doesn't help that the Colts can't seem to generate sacks and takeaways consistently. They are not worth streaming right now in fantasy.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Spencer Shrader has 8 kicking points in loss
items.desc: Spencer Shrader hit both of his field goal attempts and both PATs in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
items.impact: Shrader continued his impressive streak of scoring, albeit a little less than the output he's been producing recently. Keep him in lineups as a top-tier kicking option.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Chuba Hubbard totals 120 yards, score vs. Eagles
items.desc: Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard recorded 120 yards on 28 carries and caught one pass for one yard, punching in a rushing touchdown in a Week 6 win over Philadelphia.
items.impact: Hubbard's Week 6 outing was a season high in carries; the count has increased every single week. His rushing touchdown was his fourth this season and sixth overall. Hubbard has more than delivered on his draft capital and has been a main feature for Carolina, dominating the backfield touches.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Seth McGowan runs for 27 yards in loss
items.desc: Seth McGowan ran four times for 27 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
items.impact: McGowan is once again playing backup to Jonathan Taylor, which is unlikely to change. Keep him stashed on your bench if you have Taylor.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Deion Burks goes for 41 yards in loss to Titans
items.desc: Deion Burks caught both of his targets for 41 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday. He also ran once for seven yards.
items.impact: The rookie had only caught one of four targets on the season leading into Sunday, but he put up a nice splash play for 36 yards. He could work his way into a larger workload if the Colts find his ability as a deep threat is superior to that of Laquon Treadwell.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Laquon Treadwell brings in two passes in loss
items.desc: Laquon Treadwell caught two of five targets for 21 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
items.impact: Treadwell continued his trend of catching fewer than 50% of his targets. He's not a great option for fantasy in any format, failing to produce anything even in a depleted pass-catching room.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Bryce Young tosses pair of scores in Week 6 win
items.desc: Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young completed 20 of 39 passes for 281 yards and two touchdowns against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6.
items.impact: Young delivered against a talented Philly defense with his fourth multi-touchdown game in five weeks. He has two scores and no turnovers in each of the last two games, emerging from the Week 5 bye with the same flair. Young has at least 280 passing yards in every game, giving him an impressive floor at quarterback.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Keenan Allen grabs eight passes in loss to Titans
items.desc: Keenan Allen caught 8 of 11 targets for 82 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
items.impact: Allen led the Colts in targets, receptions, and yards in the upset loss. It's a vintage performance for Allen, but if Tyler Warren, who missed this game, is back for Week 7, it will likely signal a downturn in volume for the veteran. However, even so, he's been usable each of the last three weeks, and that trend will likely continue.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Josh Downs snags four passes in loss
items.desc: Josh Downs caught four of eight targets for 40 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday. He also ran the ball once for seven yards.
items.impact: Downs once again had a healthy target share, but didn't have a big day, even with Tyler Warren missing the game. Keenan Allen seemed to be the primary beneficiary of Warren's absence. Downs will need to show fantasy managers he can do more to be worth starting in lineups on a regular basis.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jonathan Taylor runs for 94 yards in loss
items.desc: Jonathan Taylor ran 21 times for 94 yards and a touchdown while also bringing in two of four targets for 57 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
items.impact: Taylor has been one of the few bright spots in what has been a bad season so far for the Colts. He's been a touchdown machine this year and the primary option of the offense. Expect that to continue, and the fantasy points to roll in.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Daniel Jones struggles immensely in loss
items.desc: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-42 passes for 269 yards, a touchdown, and two picks in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday. He also ran three times for 30 yards.
items.impact: On the one hand, it was good to see Jones put up some rushing numbers. On the other hand, mistakes once again hindered his performance, with two picks and six sacks sullying his day. It was his best fantasy performance of the season, though that's not saying much. He's been a disaster this year and a contributing factor to the Colts' 2-4 start.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Denver Broncos D/ST rack up turnovers in win
items.desc: The Denver Broncos D/ST racked up five sacks, two interceptions, and a fumble recovery in the team's 17-14 OT win over Seattle on Thursday.
items.impact: Denver's defense put the clamps on Seattle's offense, allowing only a single touchdown all game and a pair of field goals. The offense didn't do them many favors in sustaining drives and putting up points to give the defense a bit of breathing room, but it didn't matter. Denver's D looks like they've found their groove and will be an elite unit once again.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Wil Lutz has five kicking points in win
items.desc: Wil Lutz hit his only field goal and both of his PATs in the Broncos' 17-14 win over Seattle on Thursday.
items.impact: Lutz sealed the win for the Broncos in overtime with his kick, not seeing the field much more than that since the offense struggled to move the ball for the majority of the game. It wasn't a great night for the Broncos' offense, but better days will come for them and for Lutz to put up points.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Courtland Sutton catches two passes in win
items.desc: Courtland Sutton caught two of three targets for 19 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
items.impact: Sutton was quiet in this game, though there wasn't much to go around when the team combined for 107 passing yards. It's been a rough start to the year for QB Bo Nix, and until he improves, the pass catchers will suffer.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Evan Engram catches two passes in win
items.desc: Evan Engram caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over Seattle on Thursday.
items.impact: Engram had a nice grab in this game, but that was about it for his highlights. He should not be started in any format right now.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: RJ Harvey bounces back in Thursday win
items.desc: RJ Harvey ran six times for 25 yards and a touchdown while also catching three of four targets for 31 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over Seattle on Thursday.
items.impact: After going silent in Week 5, Harvey got back on track in Week 6, scoring a touchdown and even leading the Broncos in receiving. That last bit is a huge indictment of the Broncos' passing game, which has struggled mightily this year. Harvey is an RB3 at best right now, but if you have other options with a more stable floor who can start, that's likely the best course of action.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jaylen Waddle disappoints in win over Seattle
items.desc: Jaylen Waddle caught four of seven targets for 24 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
items.impact: Waddle has been a disappointment this season, no way around it. He's not producing, so you can't start him, but you know the potential he holds, so you can't drop him. It's a tough situation for fantasy managers to be in, so do what is best for your roster. If you can afford to hold and not start Waddle, do so. But if you need help, Waddle could be a cut candidate.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Audric Estime scores in Browns debut
items.desc: Cleveland Browns running back Audric Estimé scored a touchdown in his debut, carrying the ball nine times for 19 yards.
items.impact: Estimé's fourth-quarter touchdown tied the game for Cleveland with eight minutes left, punching it in from 2 yards out. He split the work with Jaleel McLaughlin (nine carries, four receptions) as Cleveland dealt with several running back injuries. His outlook for Week 7 is dependent on Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson's health.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: J.K. Dobbins punches in touchdown in win
items.desc: J.K. Dobbins ran 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in Denver's 17-14 win over Seattle on Thursday. He also caught three passes for five yards.
items.impact: Dobbins wasn't overly efficient in this game, with his long run of 16 yards meaning his other 16 carries went for 25 yards. Still, a touchdown and a few receptions can cover a multitude of sins. He's a volume-based RB3 moving forward.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Bo Nix struggles in win over Seattle
items.desc: Bo Nix completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards and ran four times for two yards in the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks.
items.impact: Nix was not having a great game, averaging just 4 yards per attempt in the win. He's been a very shaky player so far this season, but has managed the game well enough for the defense to pull them through to wins. He's a low-end QB2 at best until he shows signs of life.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Seattle Seahawks D/ST stifles Denver despite loss
items.desc: The Seattle Seahawks D/ST managed two sacks in the team's 17-14 loss to Denver.
items.impact: They didn't put much else up on the box score, but they largely played a good game, with both of the Broncos' touchdown drives coming in the second quarter, and largely being shut down besides that. They'll have better fantasy performances in the coming weeks.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Jerry Jeudy paces Cleveland in yards in Week 6
items.desc: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy caught four passes for a team-high 69 yards in a Week 6 win against Baltimore.
items.impact: Jeudy had his biggest game of the season so far, catching every target for a season-high in yardage. His name has been thrown around in trade rumors after the Browns' rookie wideouts started strong, but he has value as the team's WR3, even if he is not a reliable fantasy producer.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jason Myers has big miss in loss to Denver
items.desc: Jason Myers hit two of three field goal attempts in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos on Thursday. He did not attempt a PAT.
items.impact: Meyers had a miss in the third quarter that ended up being crucial in the game, as the game went to overtime tied 14-14. Had Meyers connected, it's entirely possible the Seahawks pull off the low-scoring win. However, history is history, and the only thing he can do is move on.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Velus Jones Jr. sees five touches in loss
items.desc: Velus Jones Jr. ran four times for 20 yards and caught his only target for -1 yard in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos.
items.impact: Jones was a bit of a surprise in the backfield, but he had some success running the ball in his limited touches. However, it's unlikely that he will become anything more than a gadget player, limiting any sort of upside he possesses.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Cooper Kupp goes for 50 yards in loss
items.desc: Cooper Kupp caught five of ten targets for 50 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
items.impact: Kupp had arguably his best game of the season, with season-highs in targets, receptions, and yards, lacking only a touchdown. He is a bit of a risky start most weeks, as his volume has been low for the most part. A near 20% target share this week is a nice sign of life, but we will need to see more consistency to really feel comfortable starting him.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: KC Concepcion Jr. catches four passes in Week 6
items.desc: Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion Jr. caught four passes for 37 yards in the team's Week 6 win against Baltimore.
items.impact: Concepcion caught at least four passes for the fourth time in six weeks to open his career. He has been steadily involved in Cleveland's offense, earning five or more targets in all but one week, though he has only exceeded 50 yards once. A big week could be coming soon for the Browns' dynamic receiver, as the team has prioritized giving him touches.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: AJ Barner catches three passes in loss
items.desc: AJ Barner caught three of four targets for 16 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
items.impact: Barner hasn't really gotten going this season after showing a lot of promise in 2025. The ability is there; we saw it back in Week 3 against Washington, but the opportunity hasn't been. He's not startable in fantasy right now.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Rashid Shaheed snags five passes in loss
items.desc: Rashid Shaheed caught five of eight targets for 66 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to Denver on Thursday. He also caught a two-point conversion and fumbled twice, losing one of them.
items.impact: Shaheed struggled at times in this game with ball security, but also had some nice grabs downfield and in the short area. It's a bit of a mixed bag for the veteran, but hopefully this is a sign of more involvement in the passing game and Shaheed becoming more of a viable WR2 in Seattle. Granted, Sam Darnold threw 51 passes, so the 8 targets only amounted to a 15.6% target share, but we will take what we can get.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: George Holani scores touchdown in loss
items.desc: George Holani ran five times for 20 yards and a score in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos on Thursday; he was not targeted in the passing game.
items.impact: Holani returned from a short absence and immediately ate into Emanuel Wilson's workload. He got the touchdown, but did little more. He's likely irrelevant for fantasy moving forward, especially with Zach Charbonnet expected back soon.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Jaleel McLaughlin leads Browns in touches in Week 6
items.desc: Cleveland Browns running back Jaleel McLaughlin carried the ball nine times for 41 yards and caught four passes for 14 yards in a Week 6 win.
items.impact: McLaughlin and Audric Estimé led the backfield with nine carries each with Quinshon Judkins inactive and Dylan Sampson and Rocket Sanders on injured reserve. With four receptions, he tied for the team lead too. Estimé scored the touchdown, but McLaughlin's expanded role could be just for the week.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Emanuel Wilson goes for 52 yards in loss
items.desc: Emanuel Wilson ran 14 times for 52 yards and failed to catch his only target in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
items.impact: Wilson had two weeks as the primary running back option for the Seahawks and produced in those chances. But with the return of George Holani, that window of production came to a close. Wilson still lead the backfield in touches, but he didn't get the passing or rushing work to himself like he needed. And with the return of Zach Charbonnet looming and Jadarian Price's return soon to follow after that, Wilson's usage period is coming to a close.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Sam Darnold struggles in loss to Denver
items.desc: Sam Darnold completed 27-of-51 passes for 278 yards and two interceptions in the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday. He also ran twice for 19 yards.
items.impact: It was not a good night for Darnold, whose performance led to questions of benching, which HC Mike MacDonald quickly shut down. Darnold is still the Seahawks starter, but more will be asked and expected of him in the coming weeks as Seattle looks to right the ship.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Harold Fannin Jr. catches one pass in Week 6
items.desc: Cleveland Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. was limited to one reception for nine yards on three targets in Week 6.
items.impact: Fannin had his second consecutive week with just one catch after averaging 5.0 receptions and 1.0 touchdowns from Weeks 2-4. Deshaun Watson has been held to under 175 passing yards in three of the last four weeks, putting a lid on the team's aerial output.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues crazy start to season in loss to Denver
items.desc: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
items.impact: JSN had himself a night against the Broncos' defense, though he got off to a quiet start. He has 717 yards through six games, a blistering pace of 2,031 receiving yards. He had almost 1,800 receiving yards last year, and if he can match or exceed that in 2026, it would be truly incredible.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Denzel Boston logs one catch in Week 6
items.desc: Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston logged a season low in receptions (one) with 15 yards in a Week 6 win over Baltimore.
items.impact: Boston has been a high point for Cleveland's offense, recording 40+ yards in the first five games to open his career. The rookie was still involved, earning five targets, though the opportunities did not translate into production. He should have another opportunity for a spike week against Tennessee in Week 7.

items.author: Jordan Epp
items.title: Deshaun Watson quiet in Week 6 win
items.desc: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson completed 16 of his 26 passes for 164 scoreless yards in a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 6. He added eight carries and 29 yards on the ground.
items.impact: Watson has led the Browns to an AFC North-leading 4-2 start, including a 3-0 record at home. Week 6 was his first without a touchdown and his third game in the last four weeks with fewer than 175 passing yards. The Browns' offense has not been high-octane, and Watson has provided the fantasy output of a QB2.

items.author: Joshua Kellem
items.title: Chargers D/ST Allows 22 Points in Week 6
items.desc: The Los Angeles Chargers' defense allowed 22 points and 422 total yards in a Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
items.impact: Los Angeles intercepted Patrick Mahomes once but had no answer for Kenneth Walker III, who ran for 128 yards and two touchdowns. The Chargers failed to sack Mahomes and allowed Kansas City to average 7.4 yards per play. This isn't a defense fantasy managers need to prioritize outside of favorable matchups.

items.author: Joshua Kellem
items.title: Cameron Dicker Scores Chargers' Only Points in Week 6
items.desc: Cameron Dicker made both of his field-goal attempts in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs in Week 6.
items.impact: Dicker connected from 23 and 30 yards for all six of Los Angeles' points. He did his job when called upon, but the Chargers' inability to consistently reach scoring range limits his fantasy ceiling.

items.author: Joshua Kellem
items.title: KeAndre Lambert-Smith Catches Five Passes in Week 6
items.desc: KeAndre Lambert-Smith caught five passes for 32 yards in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs in Week 6.
items.impact: Lambert-Smith didn't do much with his opportunities, but five receptions are notable in a Chargers receiving corps dealing with multiple injuries. He's worth monitoring in deeper leagues, especially if Ladd McConkey is forced to miss time, but there isn't enough here yet to trust him in fantasy lineups.
